title: Andreae, Chymische Hochzeit Christiani Rosencreutz, Strassburg 1616: printed secret-script inscriptions (DECODE R4502)

steps.what: Repo and web search for R4502 / Andreae cipher; no decipherment found under that description.
Fetched DECODE record, metadata and 8 public images; identified the item as a printed copy of the Chymische Hochzeit, not a letter.
The p.95 and p.97 inscriptions are the texts the page boy speaks on pp.96 and 98; tested as a simple substitution.
Aligned BEGRABEN, FRAW, GLUCK, FRUCHT, BAUMS etc.; built a 20-sign table consistent over both inscriptions.
DTA and 12koerbe omit the inscriptions; crcsite.org (Foxcroft 1690) footnotes all four, sign lines as 1378 and 1459.
decode.py over ciphertext.txt reproduces both German texts; date lines checked structurally against 1378/1459 (M, CCCC, IX, XX, V visible).

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): ciphertext.txt (letter inscriptions pp. 95, 97; the two date sign lines are described in NOTES, not transcribed sign by sign) and reading.txt (decode.py output); the readings of all four inscriptions copied verbatim from NOTES.md to texts/R4502_decryption.md; key.tsv as key file.

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The 20-sign table was rebuilt from the images by aligning the two inscriptions (pp. 95, 97) with the novel's own clear glosses in the paragraph after each one (pp. 96, 98); Foxcroft 1690 and the crcsite.org edition give the same readings.
outcome.fraction_read_source: reading.txt: 168 cipher letters (counted by hand from ciphertext.txt: 78 + 90) of the two letter inscriptions, all given values; the two date lines read as wholes (graded C)
outcome.notes: Not a letter: DECODE's four cipher pages are the printed inscriptions of the novel, which glosses its own two long ones. Per-sign values in the two symbolic date lines stay graded C.

credits.note: English readings of the inscriptions (1690), via the crcsite.org edition; the two date lines (1378, 1459) taken from it
credits.source: Foxcroft, The Hermetick Romance (London 1690); crcsite.org edition

texts.label: Chymische Hochzeit (1616), inscriptions pp. 73, 95, 97, 116
texts.summary: The secret-script inscriptions of Andreae's novel Chymische Hochzeit Christiani Rosencreutz (Strassburg 1616), not a letter: the copper door of Venus's vault ('here lies buried Venus, the fair woman who has brought many a high man to ruin of fortune, honour, blessing and welfare') and the tablet behind her bed (when the fruit of my tree is fully melted, I shall awake and be the mother of a king). The novel glosses both itself; the two sign lines on pp. 73 and 116 read as the dates 1378 and 1459 (graded C).

prior.where: The novel itself (glosses on pp. 96, 98); Foxcroft, The Hermetick Romance (1690), as footnoted on crcsite.org.
